title: The Neighbouring Families

full_text:
In a quiet garden, two families lived on either side of a wooden fence: the sparrows nesting under the eaves, and the roses blooming in the parterre. For generations, the sparrows chirped that the roses were vain, ornamental creatures who did no useful work, while the roses turned their petals away, calling the sparrows noisy, dusty scavengers.

Yet when a fierce winter storm froze the earth, a young sparrow fell half-frozen among the thorn bushes, and the rose stalks sheltered the shivering bird from the icy blast. In the spring, the sparrow cleared destructive caterpillars from the tender rose buds.

Looking upon each other with new eyes, the neighbors realized that nature creates each being with a vital role to play, and that true community thrives when differences are respected with mutual goodwill.
moral: Prejudice between families is dissolved when mutual kindness and simple humanity triumph over gossip.
